Copy tweaks, constant changes, comment-level micro-edits — the target spot is clear and no logic branches are involved. Fastest tier to run (iterations x0.8, earlier compaction), but the model does no upfront reasoning at all, so slightly complex tasks can go badly wrong; fall back to LIGHT when unsure.

Single-spot small changes: one function, one config block, one style tweak — the blast radius is obvious at a glance. The glance-edit discipline (scan before editing, scan the diff after) is enough to cover the risk, and the only cost is a 256-token thinking budget — the default for everyday small fixes.

Regular feature changes: one complete but bounded mini-requirement (add a validation, cover a branch, wire a callback). The standard read → edit → verify → re-read loop plus minimal-diff discipline, at a moderate cost. Escalate to DEEP once a change spans more than two files.

Multi-file features or changes with ripple effects: build the changeset list before touching anything, tie every change to a verification, and delegate exploratory work to code_task sub-agents. Tool failures automatically append a self-check. Costs start to matter (iterations x1.2), but it prevents editing A and forgetting B.

Danger-zone refactors: core data structures, shared utility functions, state-machine transitions — one broken invariant cascades into a chain of bugs. Invariant identification, ripple-effect review and the final three-question checklist are all enabled, at iterations x1.5. Worth it only where a wrong edit costs more to roll back than the thinking does.

Cross-module deep changes: one edit ripples into three or more modules, or you must map the whole call chain before starting. The coding loop of dependency map → candidate edits → risk ranking → minimal change → immediate verification → regression sweep, at iterations x2.0 with an output budget of 12000 — several times the token cost of STANDARD, in exchange for verified edits and no regression debt.

Architecture-scale changes: framework swaps, data-layer migrations, redrawing module boundaries — the kind of work where a wrong edit sinks the project. Impact-radius mapping, a multi-option comparison matrix, adversarial self-review, a full verification matrix and evidence-chain reporting, at iterations x3.0, budget 65536, with later compaction preserving the full evidence chain — the cost ceiling of the whole ladder. Reserve it for genuinely big jobs: enabling it for daily tasks just burns tokens.

Pick this when unsure: the engine re-picks the tier each turn from task complexity (length, multi-step indicators, code content, risk words, error history) — simple questions drop to NONE instantly, and deep-water situations auto-escalate to ULTRACODE. It never auto-picks APEXCODE (the cost guardrail); the top tier must always be chosen manually.
